steps.what: Browse new music releases and trend sources in music-library and discovery software {OTHER}; configure native label, artist and release-date filters to reduce repeated navigation while checking the original release information.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of music releases and trends by listening closely, comparing styles, observing audience response and exchanging views with other music professionals.

tasks.design: Configure native release views in music discovery software {OTHER}. Reduce repeated catalogue navigation while keeping listening, cultural interpretation and professional conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Following several catalogues can repeat the same browsing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing catalogue filters can surface releases from selected sources.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish a useful musical direction from a transient popularity signal.
tasks.human_edge: Hear how a track might work with a particular audience.
tasks.altitude: Less catalogue navigation; the listening and taste-building work remains.

evidence.claim: Music catalogue filters can narrow release browsing but do not establish artistic relevance.

assumptions: Boundary is routine discovery and listening, not set preparation, track purchases or a report. Shares are illustrative. No routine written report or send is assumed for this knowledge task.

Catalogue publishers supply track/artist, release date, label and preview availability. The DJ supplies existing interests and verifies catalogue details during s1; missing metadata requires ordinary source browsing, counted there. No free curated shortlist is assumed.
Native filtering precedes code. Existing recommendations or background scans earn no labour credit. If current filters already work, the saving is zero; listening and conversations retain full time.
research_questions: Does a native release view remove navigation without narrowing discovery excessively?

already_counted.description: Source browsing checks and all listening and interpretation remain in s1-s2.

incremental.description: Refresh source filters and inspect omitted releases.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10 less 1 upkeep gives 9, limited to repeated source navigation; zero if current discovery views already suffice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Mix, cut and sample recorded music

steps.what: Select and audition recorded music on DJ controllers and mixing software {OTHER}, checking the actual track, usable section, levels and intended transition through the private cue channel.

Prepare and check the next mix, cut or sample on the private cue bus using DJ mixers and performance software {OTHER}, listening to the actual prepared audio and choosing its entry point and level before routing it to the audience.
outputs: checked next audio cue and routing choice

steps.what: Mix, cut or sample the checked recorded music through the DJ controller and mixer {OTHER} into the public output, performing the chosen transition and responding directly to the sound and audience.
inputs: checked next audio cue and routing choice

tasks.design: Keep the controller and mixer performance in {OTHER} with the DJ. Existing cueing and playback functions already support the work; this design adds no automation or saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on artistic timing and listening during performance.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing private cueing is sufficient; no new enabler is claimed.
tasks.still_hard: Make an expressive transition in a changing room.
tasks.human_edge: Shape energy and timing through live musical judgement.

ambition.what: No new service or decision rights.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the performance week.

evidence.claim: Private cueing supports a performer's immediate listening check before a source reaches the public mix.

assumptions: Boundary is the live mixing cycle, including private preparation and actual public audio routing. Shares are illustrative. No mandatory manual performance log, report or record commit is invented; any automatic play-history runtime is not human work.

The DJ chooses the actual source file, cue section, timing, levels and output routing in s1-s2, listening through the controller's private bus. Missing or unsuitable audio requires another selection and audition within those steps. No free prepared playlist is assumed.

Native cueing and controller functions were considered and are already present; no remaining manual duplication was found after separating private preparation and public output. The immediate s2 cue check is ordinary performance activity, not extra approval time.

The graph repeats for each next audible cue. a1 binds that actual checked source/cue/routing choice, not a blanket future set. Changing it requires a fresh private cue check. Public performance remains fully human and retains all time.
research_questions: Is any actual manual edit export required outside this live-performance boundary?

already_counted.description: Source audition, private cue preparation/check and public performance remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: No change is introduced, so there is no additional upkeep.

approvals.approved_version: Actual next audio source, cue and routing checked in the immediately preceding s2 cycle

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All current audition, cue preparation and live output retain full effort. Existing playback functions do not create new labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advertise DJ services online and in brochures

steps.what: Choose the audience, service offer, available dates, spending limit and online or brochure channels for advertising the DJ's actual services, checking existing booking details and image permissions.
Write the advertising copy and choose examples and imagery that accurately describe the music service and suit the audience.

Lay out the online advertisement in {ADS} and brochure in design software {OTHER}; configure native reusable sizes, styles and contact fields to reduce repeated layout, checking each rendered output for clipping and legibility.

Check the finished advertisement and brochure for truthful claims, actual availability, contact details and image permissions, and verify the final online audience, dates, spending limit, print quantity and intended distribution.
outputs: checked final publicity package and delivery settings

steps.what: Save the checked final advertisement and brochure files in {DOCS}.
inputs: checked final publicity package and delivery settings

steps.what: Publish the checked final online advertisement with the verified audience, dates and spending limit in {ADS}.
inputs: checked final publicity package and delivery settings

steps.what: Send the checked final brochure file and print quantity to the existing print provider using {EMAIL}.
inputs: checked final publicity package and delivery settings

steps.what: Check the received brochures against the approved artwork and distribute the correct copies at the intended venues or events, handling actual venue permission and audience interactions.
inputs: checked final publicity package and delivery settings

tasks.design: Use native templates in {ADS} and design software {OTHER} for repeated online and brochure layout. Keep offer decisions, original copy, completed-output checks and physical distribution, with separate gates on saving, publishing and issuing the print request.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated format and contact-field setup can slow each promotion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reusable formats can retain standard layout without generating claims.
tasks.still_hard: Represent the service honestly and appeal to the right audience.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a credible musical identity and build venue relationships.

ambition.what: No new channel or spending authority.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated layout work with the same publicity and budget responsibility.

evidence.claim: Reusable advertising and design templates can reduce repeated layout setup without replacing copy judgement or physical distribution.

assumptions: Boundary covers the DJ's advertising work for an existing mixed online/brochchure campaign. Shares are illustrative, not measured; printer production is existing supplier work and earns no focal labour saving. Printed copies are the supplier's response to s7, not an input assumed before the request.

DJ supplies actual offer, contact details, target audience, budget, dates and print quantity in s1; booking records and authorised asset files supply availability and permissions. Missing details require manual clarification in s1. Copy is actually written in s2, not supplied free.
Native templates are tested first. Only repeated size, style and field setup loses time. Existing template runtime, ordinary saves/sends, supplier printing and physical distribution earn no saving.

s4 is the normal finished-publicity check, not added approval work. Its gates bind the final artwork and delivery settings; edits invalidate them. s8 checks physical copies against that exact artwork and does not distribute changed or misprinted material.
unknowns: Actual channel mix and manual layout effort
research_questions: Which repeated layout actions remain after using current native templates?

already_counted.description: Brief, copy, retained layout checks, final check, save, releases and physical distribution remain in s1-s8.

incremental.description: Refresh contact and format templates and check platform changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final advertising and brochure files checked in s4
Final online artwork, audience, dates and budget checked in s4
Final brochure artwork, print quantity and provider checked in s4
Same approved brochure artwork and distribution destinations checked in s4, with copy conformity checked in s8

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 12.5 less 1.5 upkeep gives 11. Upper case removes repeated format setup; zero when current templates already remove it. Physical brochure work remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The DJ keeps taste, live performance and publicity choices while native catalogue and design views reduce selected preparation work.
reach: Coordinate monitoring with sound engineering technicians
role.ambitious_version: Give the DJ more time for listening and audience connection without automating the performance.
